title: Will Nifty, Sensex fall for 6th straight session on Monday? US Fed among 5 factors to watch this week
summary: Indian equity benchmarks have fallen for multiple sessions, with Sensex down over 2,000 points in five days and Nifty closing below 23,800. Market participants are watching five key factors this week, including the US Federal Reserve decision, technical charts, foreign institutional investor flows, geopolitical ripples from the Gulf, and a heavy slate of corporate earnings. Several large-cap and select small-cap stocks are in focus amid renewed volatility.
content:
Will Nifty and Sensex extend losses to a sixth straight session on Monday? Indian markets have shown significant weakness, with Sensex slipping more than 2,000 points across five trading sessions and Nifty closing below the key 23,800 support level. Market commentary points to several reasons for the pullback as participants brace for another volatile week.

Traders and investors should watch five key factors this week. First is the US Federal Reserve decision and its policy guidance, which could influence global risk appetite and capital flows into Indian equities. Second are technical charts and momentum indicators after the recent sharp decline; analysts are assessing how deep and prolonged the correction could be. Third, flows from foreign institutional investors matter: FIIs recently injected about $3 billion into Indian stocks, but future buying or selling will be closely tracked. Fourth, geopolitical developments — including ripples from the Gulf — have added uncertainty and pressured markets. Fifth, a heavy calendar of corporate earnings, especially from the technology and large-cap sectors, could shape sentiment.

Several headlines and stock-specific stories are drawing attention. Radhakishan Damani picked up a stake in an NBFC that had fallen sharply in 2026. Reports highlighted that some smallcaps delivered very high returns year to date as FIIs raised stakes in selective names. High-profile corporate news includes potential acquisitions and regulatory actions, while specific stocks in the spotlight include Infosys, Cipla, Meesho, Suzlon Energy, IndiGo and NTPC.

Market strategists point to a mix of fundamental and technical pressures: profit-taking, rising yields and geopolitical news have amplified downside moves. While some institutional flows have come in recently, the pace and sustainability of buying remain uncertain. Analysts recommend watching support and resistance levels on the charts, monitoring FII behavior, and tracking US policy signals and corporate earnings for clues on direction.

For investors, the week presents mixed signals: opportunities in beaten-down names exist alongside elevated risk. Short-term traders may focus on volatility and sector rotations, while longer-term investors are advised to assess fundamentals and valuations amid shifting macro cues. The coming days will likely determine whether the recent selloff deepens or stabilizes.

(Notes: headlines and market lists referenced include trending topics such as SBI, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, Infosys, Wipro and NTPC share prices, and commentary on multibagger smallcaps and large-cap stock recommendations.)
